title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building 'Teichmüller groupoids' S0T as full subgroupoids of fundamental groupoids of spaces SP^Y_G of genus-0 marked configurations with tangential data. The base points are chosen in sets E_{G,Q}, which are torsors under groups such as {±1}^{A_1}×{±1}^{J_III}. The previous page treats the generic case, where SP^Y_G ≅ 𝕌^{Â} ∧^{γ_G} E_{G,Q}. Here 𝕌 is the circle group.

On this page he begins reviewing the exceptional Y, i.e. marked spheres (Y,I) with extra automorphisms. The first case is |I| = 4 with the stabiliser of a marked point i of order 3. Equivalently, Aut(Y,I) is the alternating group 𝔖_I^+ ≅ A_4. The configuration is then the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron inscribed in the oriented Riemann sphere. This is the equianharmonic configuration (cross-ratio −ω or −ω², j = 0). There are two such labelled configurations, matching the two orientations of I (the two A_4-classes of orderings).

The isotropy group G_i of a vertex i is cyclic of order 3. It acts on the tangent line T_iY by a faithful character, which gives a canonical identification G_i ≅ μ3 = μ3(ℂ) ≅ ℤ/3. G_i permutes the other three points cyclically, so η_i := I∖{i} is a μ3-torsor.

Each j ∈ η_i determines a tangent direction at i: the geodesic or symmetry arc from i to j. This gives a μ3-equivariant map η_i → (circle of directions at i). Hence the 𝕌-torsor J_i of tangential directions at i is canonically the induced torsor J_i ≅ 𝕌 ×^{μ3} η_i, via the canonical inclusion μ3 ↪ 𝕌.

Purpose: in the exceptional (orbifold) case the {±1}-type base-point torsors of the generic case are replaced by μ3-torsors. These are canonical tangential base points at the order-3 orbifold point of M_{0,4}, which feed into the description of S0T for exceptional Y. The page breaks off ('On…'). The next page starts a new section ('Graphes MD').
errors: No mathematical error. Only an implicit point: the identification G_i ≅ μ3 must be made through the tangent representation at i, not through an abstract isomorphism to ℤ/3, for the formula J_i ≅ 𝕌 ×^{μ3} η_i to be canonical. Grothendieck writes μ3(ℂ), which suggests he intends this.

ideas.what: Characterisation of the exceptional 4-pointed sphere with automorphism group A_4 as the tetrahedral (equianharmonic) configuration; two labelled copies correspond to the two orientations of I
ideas.modern_name: orbifold point of order 3 of M_{0,4}/S_4 (j=0, cross-ratio −ω)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to using curves with extra symmetries as base points for Teichmüller groupoids

ideas.what: Canonical μ3-torsor of 'directions toward the other marked points' at a vertex, and the circle of tangent directions as its induced 𝕌-torsor
ideas.modern_name: canonical tangential base points at orbifold points / torsor induction
ideas.usually_credited_to: tangential base points: Deligne (1989), Ihara, Nakamura; specific symmetric choices: various (e.g. Nakamura–Schneps work on Teichmüller tower)

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts a systematic case list of exceptional Y (spheres with extra automorphisms) to serve as rigid, canonically-torsored base points for genus-0 Teichmüller groupoids. Only the tetrahedral case is begun; the remaining cases (e.g. the order-2/square configuration) and the resulting groupoid presentation are not written.
missed.quote: Je vais d'abord passer en revue les cas de Y exceptionnels
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Symmetric base points at orbifold points are used ad hoc in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature. A systematic treatment via μ_n-torsors of directions is a modest but clean viewpoint; it is unlikely to be new in substance.

deep.surprise_reason: Classical geometry of the equianharmonic 4-point configuration, plus a natural torsor formalism for tangential base points. It matches Grothendieck's known program (Esquisse) and contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Je vais d'abord passer en revue les cas de Y exceptionnels' rather than 'passer en dimension aux cas'.
The displayed formula is likely 'J_i ≃ 𝕌 ×^{μ3} η_i' (J_i = circle-torsor of directions, 𝕌 = circle group as on the previous page), not 'I_i ≃ M ×^{μ3} η_i'.
The last line reads '[où] μ3 ↪ 𝕌 est l'inclusion canonique'.
Configurations are 'circonscrites au tétraèdre [régulier]', i.e. the sphere circumscribed to the regular tetrahedron; 'les 2 possibilités correspondant aux deux orientations de I'.
